title: Split and Bridge: Multimodal Generation via Diffusion Bridging
claim: Independent pretrained generators can be coupled by sharing one trajectory, then branching at a split point via a bridge intervention.
layout: 2 panels: left bridge-variant list, right trajectory heatmap with sample images on top
description: The figure has two parts. On the left is a gray box titled 'Bridge B'. It holds four rounded sub-boxes, each with a score-function equation showing how the bridge intervenes: change prompt (c1 to c2), change model (x(1) to x(2)), change layers (θ to θ+Δθ'), and a pink 'Learnable Bridge' box with the regression loss. Purple marks modality 1 and red marks modality 2. On the right, a viridis-colored heatmap shows a noisy purple trajectory that follows a shared path from t=1. At t_split it forks, and a 'Bridge B' box redirects it into a red trajectory that diverges downward. The time axis runs from 1 to 0 along the bottom. Above the heatmap are output pairs: rabbit and dog images, and a face mask and face photo. Each pair is labeled x̂(1) or x̂(2).
caption: SnB leverages pretrained diffusion models by coupling reverse trajectories during sampling. We start from a common state sampled from a prior, then at tsplit, a bridge module is used to implement a score intervention on the reverse process. This intervention can be through modifying conditioning signals (e.g., prompts), changing diffusion models that estimate the score functions, or changing certain layers in the diffusion models. This flexibility applies SnB in various tasks, like interleaved co-generation (top left pair) and multimodal generation (top right pair). Learnable bridges allows stronger trajectory manipulation in mapping one modality to another.
abstract: Visual data are often expressed through multiple complementary modalities (e.g., images and segmentation masks), each capturing different aspects of the same underlying structure. Most existing multimodal methods adopt a top-down paradigm, learning a shared latent variable through joint training from scratch, which limits scalability. We propose Split and Bridge (SnB), a bottom-up framework for multimodal generation that couples pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time. Rather than learning a unified latent space, SnB generates coherent multimodal samples by following a shared diffusion trajectory up to a split point and then branching into modality-specific trajectories guided by a bridge module. This design enables plug-and-play reuse of powerful pretrained models without joint training, making it scalable and easily adaptable. Across standard benchmarks (PolyMNIST, CelebAMask-HQ) and more complex settings (PIE-Bench++, ROCO), SnB achieves a strong balance between sample quality and coherence. We show that SnB naturally extends to downstream zero-shot tasks such as interleaved co-generation, image editing, and style coupling/decoupling. Our results demonstrate that bottom-up generation provides a practical framework that complements existing top-down multimodal approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/AhmadArrabi/SnB
